lens: LEGAL & PROVENANCE: license validity, redistribution of EA IP, possible derivation from proprietary Chrono Divide code, auditability of the history

refuted_claims.claim: The GPL-3.0-or-later licence on the project code is unambiguous. Game files are outside the repo ('not supplied in the source repository'). The only asset with unclear licensing is the startup background.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The repo itself commits EA-copyrighted artwork that is neither GPL nor disclosed. scripts/assets/extractIcon.mts says it extracts icon resources 'from the original game's PE32'. Its outputs are committed in the init commit aa1eef8: public/favicon.ico, favicon-192.png, favicon-512.png, favicon-maskable-512.png, apple-touch-icon.png and public/icons/ra2.png and yr.png. I viewed them: they are the RA2 Soviet-star game icon and the YR Yuri emblem. docs/THIRD_PARTY.md does not list them. The background jpg looks AI-generated. It carries the 'RA2' mark and an Apocalypse tank and Kirov silhouette, and the docs themselves say it has no licence.
refuted_claims.correction: The GPL applies to the original TS/JS code only. The repo also ships unlicensed EA icon art taken from game.exe, plus a background of unknown licence. Before any derivative is published, all of these must be removed or replaced.

refuted_claims.claim: The executables come from a 'third-party host' (oldgame.store).
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The registry whois (whois.nic.store) shows oldgame.store was created on 2026-09-14T02:25:56Z at Spaceship, Inc. That is the same day as the 'init OSS release' commit aa1eef8 (2026-09-14 21:14 +0800). The host is a Cloudflare-fronted proxy (x-proxy-cache header). It answers GET /game.exe and /gamemd.exe with 200 and application/x-msdownload, a 4,497,680-byte game.exe, and 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *'. I checked only HEAD and status; I did not download the binaries. A domain registered for the launch and CORS-configured for this app makes it very likely the host is affiliated with the project (INFERENCE; no registrant is disclosed).
refuted_claims.correction: Treat oldgame.store as effectively first-party infrastructure that distributes EA's proprietary executables. The project is therefore the likely distributor, not a passive linker. Any derivative must drop the host completely, not just stop linking to it.

refuted_claims.claim: Legally purchased EA App/Steam executables may not work (UNVERIFIED).
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The code settles this regardless of the hash question. In src/ui/pages/game/gameSourcePicker.ts manifestGate, the comments say 'Always use the fixed compatible executable version' and 'Overlay-first: the executable overrides any same-named archive file'. The downloaded game.exe/gamemd.exe always replaces the player's own. So the README's 'prepare game resources you legally own' never applies to the executables: the app does not run a user-owned EXE at all. The pinned game.exe is an XWIS multiplayer-client build. manifest.ts derives it from 'Red_Alert_2.rar' and a multiplayer-client set, and downloadCatalog.ts points to archive.org 'Red-Alert-2-Multiplayer.exe'. It is not a retail build (INFERENCE: likely a community-modified, CD-less exe).
refuted_claims.correction: Out of the box there is no lawful execution path. To run it on your own copy you must remove the overlay and re-derive every hash-pinned address patch in src/games/ra2 and src/games/yr for your own executable, or show that your executable is byte-identical to the pinned one. That is a real engineering cost.

refuted_claims.claim: Vendored third-party code keeps its own licences (7z-wasm 'SEE LICENSE IN License.txt'), and there is no licence defect.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: node_modules/7z-wasm/License.txt says 7zz.wasm and 7zz.*.js are under 'GNU LGPL + unRAR restriction'. The unRAR clause is non-free and generally regarded as GPL-incompatible. The app bundles 7zz.wasm (1.65 MB in dist/) and uses it to extract RAR. THIRD_PARTY.md does not flag this.
refuted_claims.correction: For a distributed GPL derivative there is a licence-hygiene issue. Either drop RAR support and use a build without unRAR, or document the work as an aggregate. For purely private use it does not matter.

refuted_claims.claim: Provenance is 'original work' (stated as fully verified).
refuted_claims.why_wrong: The public history is 12 commits. The code arrives as squashed drops: aa1eef8 adds 454 files and +82,414 lines, by author 'agent <agent@anonymous.local>'. The real history lives on an unpublished 'dev' branch, and THIRD_PARTY.md cites a private 'PR #17, commit 9ae5cb6'. Authorship and any copied code can only be checked against the snapshot, not the history. I found no large or deleted binary blobs in the public history.
refuted_claims.correction: Independence from Chrono Divide is well supported by content comparison. 'Original work' in general is only confirmed at the snapshot level, and the development history is not auditable.

confirmed_claims: LICENSE is the full GNU GPL v3 text. package.json declares GPL-3.0-or-later, and the GitHub API reports spdx GPL-3.0 (gh api repos/ra2-games/ra2, 2026-09-27). The repo is not a fork; homepage is ra2.games; 238 stars and 33 forks.

The repo is not derived from Chrono Divide. There is no engine-reimplementation code. The only mentions of CD are CSS comments (styles.css lines 577, 999, 1019, 1576, 2136). After stripping comments, a declaration-level comparison against CD's style.css (provenance/cd/style.css) finds only 2 generic shared declarations out of 454 ('background-repeat: no-repeat' and 'justify-content: space-between'), so no CSS was copied verbatim. The other agent's literal and path tests (2 generic literals, 1 path 'main') support this.

src/main.ts:15 calls preloadThirdPartyFiles(...) on page load. src/games/manifest.ts registers https://oldgame.store/game.exe with a SHA-256. src/games/downloadCatalog.ts links to uc129.com, jb51.net and archive.org Red-Alert-2-Multiplayer.exe. scripts/resources/prepareThirdPartyExes.mts downloads the EXEs 'from third-party shared locations'.

EA's Feb 2025 GPL source release covered Tiberian Dawn, Red Alert, Renegade and Generals/Zero Hour, and not RA2/YR. It also grants no trademark rights (https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2025/02/ea-just-open-sourced-command-conquer-red-alert-renegade-and-generals/).

The vendored shader licences check out. SweetFX is MIT (src/graphics/vendor/sweetfx/LICENSE, (c) 2014 CeeJayDK). Anime4K is MIT, a copy of the upstream GLSL left unchanged except for SHA pinning. ScaleFX and FSR 1.0 keep their MIT headers (src/ui/pages/game/vendor/README.md). v86 is BSD-2-Clause (node_modules/v86/package.json and gh api copy/v86). No ONNX weights are committed.
src/games/yr/spawnerProbe.ts states that the CnCNet yrpp-spawner implementation 'was not copied'. Even if it had been, yrpp-spawner is GPL-3.0 (gh api), which is compatible with this repo's GPL.
The embedded original-binary bytes are only short signature/expected sequences, e.g. profile.ts 'expected: [0x8b,0x4d,0x08,0xf7,0xf1]'. This is de minimis and serves interoperability.
The git history holds no committed or deleted EXE/DLL/MIX/model blobs over 300 KB (git rev-list --all --objects scan).
CONTRIBUTORS.md lists Junlin Liu (@NoCLin), Yuyuan Li (hdu.edu.cn faculty link), Lin Zhao, Jiayuan Fang and Yifan Xu. PR #2 from Yohoa was merged by NoCLin.
verdict_notes:
From the legal and provenance lens this is the cleanest web base found so far with respect to Chrono Divide. It is also clean with respect to other GPL projects. Its own code is really GPL-3.0-or-later, independently written, and shows no CD copying at the code or CSS level. The CD-derived family (huangkaoya, OpenRA2, DD-Channel) would score roughly 1-2 on this lens.

The evaluation understates the EA-side problems, though. Three findings the original evaluation missed:
(1) The repo commits EA icon art extracted from game.exe into public/.
(2) The EXE host oldgame.store was registered on the day of the OSS release and serves the binaries with CORS * enabled. It is very likely project-affiliated (INFERENCE), which makes the project a probable distributor of unlicensed EA executables.
(3) The code always replaces the player's own EXE with the downloaded one. Running a legally owned copy is therefore impossible without code changes and re-deriving every hash-pinned patch; it is not merely 'unverified'.

Additional notes:
- The bundled 7zz.wasm carries the non-free unRAR restriction.
- YRpp, cited in docs/GAME_PERFORMANCE.md for struct layouts, has no licence (gh api Phobos-developers/YRpp license=null). Only factual layouts appear to be used, so the risk is low.
- EA's User Agreement (saved at scratchpad/ea_ua.txt) forbids reverse engineering 'unless expressly authorized by EA or permitted by law', and this project's core technique is disassembly plus binary patching. That is a gray area that depends on jurisdiction.
- EA's C&C Franchise Modding Guidelines (Revision 2, 2025-02-27; saved at scratchpad/ea_mod.txt, source URL not recorded) grant a revocable, non-commercial licence to use C&C Assets in free mods, excluding music files. That helps a personal, non-commercial, asset-replacement remaster, but it does not cover redistributing EXEs.

For a strictly private, non-distributed build using the user's own purchased copy, the risk is modest, provided three things are done: strip preloadThirdPartyFiles and the oldgame.store/downloadCatalog links, remove the extracted icons, and re-derive the patches against the user's own EXE (the EA App/Steam 1.006/1.001 builds may differ). If anything is shared publicly, the EXE-download dependency and the EA art must go first. Net legal suitability: 5/10. That is higher than the original evaluation's weighted 4 on legal grounds alone, but with stronger conditions than the evaluation stated.
